# Corporate Travel Guide: Comparing Modes for Regional Trips

For journeys of two to five hundred kilometres, companies often struggle to set a clear default travel mode. Air is fast in the air but slow at the airport, rail offers productive time but varies in price, and coaches are cheap but slow. This guide summarises what our research says about regional business travel.

## Door to door time

Published journey times rarely reflect the real experience. For flights, travellers should add time to reach the airport, pass security and travel from the destination airport into the city. For rail and coach, stations are usually central, which reduces the transfer time at both ends.

FACT: Travellers on regional flights spent an average of 2 hours on airport transfers and security.
FACT: Employees reported 74 percent productive working time on trains.
FACT: The standard corporate mileage rate in our 2026 survey was 67 cents per mile.

## Cost beyond the fare

Total trip cost includes taxis, parking, meals and lost working time. When productive time is valued, rail frequently comes out ahead of air for journeys under four hours, even when the fare is similar or slightly higher.

## Sustainability

Many companies now set carbon budgets for travel. Rail and coach emit far less per passenger than short flights, and a growing number of travel policies require employees to justify flying when a train alternative of similar duration exists.

## Recommendations

Set rail as the default for regional trips where it is competitive on time, allow air when schedules make same-day return impossible otherwise, and reserve coach travel for cost-sensitive trips where time is less critical.
